rationale: Revision 4 strengthens the architecture in the areas most material to my financial-resource and settlement review. It makes per-phase authority, replay identity and fee consumption explicit; rejects target-incompatible no-effect promises; separates domain-qualified asset conservation from typed liability evolution; and requires the authenticated effect frame rather than a convenient prover-selected subset. Its Core/constraint/ledger distinctions, arbitrary-witness obligations and explicit compiler trusted base prevent advisory solver results or native circuit verification alone from being advertised as end-to-end intention correctness. The verified hash binds this advisory endorsement. No implementation or release acceptance is claimed.
caveats: The phase-aware proof and receipt must account for every surviving guaranteed effect, fee and consumed authorization when fallible execution fails. A failure transition preserves remaining liabilities and cumulative bounds; refunds and compensation cannot erase earlier gross debits or reset work.

Asset accounting must cover all relevant accounts, custody and reserves in the authenticated frame, with explicit authorized mint/burn. The liability equation must be instantiated per typed obligation, identity, unit and debtor/creditor relation. Refinance, capitalization, write-off and novation need explicit authorized transition semantics rather than informal netting.

Proof correctness and observation authenticity remain independent. Verifying a signature or circuit over attested data does not establish external truth. The actual predecessor-consumption and finality rules remain ledger obligations, and liveness requires its named liquidity, witness and network assumptions.

The source-to-target correspondence is correctly marked unestablished. Target binding, exact keys and compiler versions provide identity, not equivalence. Per-artifact validation is useful only if its soundness and coverage support the claimed Core judgment, complete effects and target phase behavior.

I did not independently audit the PR17 Agda source, WShape definition, SubRealizer or the exact proposed old-surface ZKIR mapping during this settlement review. I endorse the explicit hostile-witness, producer and semantic-version obligations; the source-specific summaries require the designated expert evidence and must remain conditional.

Canonical signed intent may authorize bounded substitutions and partial outcomes, but a solver cannot alter those predicates or choose a weaker property relation. Private commitments must retain canonical openings and binding without assuming public disclosure of private state.
Internal Pel controls must remain internal. A service catalog, local resolver whitelist or version-selection policy cannot silently become administrative approval of supported developer programs.
evidence_that_would_change_vote: An accepted lowerer layout charging fees, consuming replay authority or creating effects outside the signed failure policy, or a receipt reporting no effects after a fallible failure with surviving guaranteed effects.
A conservation or history argument omitting fee recipients, custody, supply changes, residual liabilities or portions of the authenticated effect frame.

A satisfying hostile witness that violates source definedness, range, assertions, effects or work, or evidence that WShape/producer obligations remain assumptions while the resulting artifact is labelled semantically verified.
A compiler/ledger mismatch for the pinned ZKIR version, circuit/key interpretation or phase adapter, without a scoped rejection or correction.
An administrative public deployment allowlist or mandatory reviewer/campaign receipts for ordinary supported Moriarty programs.

Positive evidence of independently checked correspondence or sound translation validation, phase-aware rejection/partial/full-success readback, hostile-witness controls and mandatory proof-enabled Midnight acceptance would justify advancing implementation status beyond this design endorsement.
